title.en: Define surface tension and surface energy
Use the angle of contact and excess pressure

say.en: A pond skater stands on water without sinking, and a carefully placed needle floats. The surface of water behaves like a stretched skin. In this lesson: Define surface tension and surface energy.
Use the angle of contact and excess pressure.
Find capillary rise.

body.en: Molecules at a liquid surface have extra energy because they have fewer neighbours. *Surface tension* S is the force per unit length along a line on the surface, S = F/l, and it also equals the surface energy per unit area. Its unit is N m⁻¹. A liquid tries to make its surface as small as possible, which is why free drops are spherical. Detergents lower S.
body.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯ ಅಣುಗಳಿಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ. ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಎಳೆತ S = F/l, ಇದು ಏಕಮಾನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣದ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಶಕ್ತಿಗೂ ಸಮ. ಏಕಮಾನ N m⁻¹. ಹನಿಗಳು ಗೋಳಾಕಾರ; ಮಾರ್ಜಕಗಳು S ಅನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

A molecule deep inside a liquid is pulled equally on all sides. A molecule at the surface is pulled only sideways and inwards, so the surface has extra energy.
Surface tension is the force per unit length along a line in the surface. It also equals the surface energy per unit area.
The angle of contact decides the shape of the surface. Water wets clean glass, theta less than 90 degrees; mercury does not, theta more than 90 degrees.
The pressure inside a drop is more than outside by 2S over r. A soap bubble has two surfaces, so the excess is 4S over r.
In a thin glass tube, water climbs until the surface tension pull balances the weight of the column.

narration.en: Surface tension pulls the liquid up a thin tube until the column's weight balances it: h = 2S cos θ/(ρ g r). Water wets glass (θ ≈ 0) and rises; mercury does not wet glass (θ ≈ 140°) and is pushed down. A tube twice as wide gives half the rise.
narration.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಸೆಳೆತ ದ್ರವವನ್ನು ತೆಳು ನಳಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮೇಲೆಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, ಕಂಬದ ತೂಕ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮವಾಗುವವರೆಗೆ: h = 2S cos θ/(ρ g r). ನೀರು ಗಾಜನ್ನು ತೇವಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ (θ ≈ 0), ಏರುತ್ತದೆ; ಪಾದರಸ ತೇವಗೊಳಿಸದು (θ ≈ 140°), ಕೆಳಗೆ ತಳ್ಳಲ್ಪಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡು ಪಟ್ಟು ಅಗಲದ ನಳಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಏರಿಕೆ ಅರ್ಧ.

title.en: Angle of contact, drops, bubbles and capillary rise

body.en: The *angle of contact* θ is the angle between the liquid surface and the solid inside the liquid. Water on clean glass has θ < 90° and wets it; mercury has θ > 90° and does not. The pressure inside a drop exceeds the outside by 2S/r; a soap bubble has two surfaces, so 4S/r. In a capillary tube of radius r a liquid rises to h = 2S cos θ/(ρgr); mercury is depressed instead.
body.kn: ಸ್ಪರ್ಶಕೋನ θ < 90° ಆದರೆ ದ್ರವ ಗಾಜನ್ನು ತೇವಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹನಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಒತ್ತಡ 2S/r, ಸೋಪಿನ ಗುಳ್ಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ 4S/r. ಲೋಮನಾಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಏರಿಕೆ h = 2S cos θ/(ρgr).

tagline.en: Viscous drag, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, Reynolds number, surface tension, excess pressure and capillary rise.

say.en: Worked example (NCERT). A copper ball of radius 2 mm falls through oil at a terminal speed of 6.5 cm/s. $\rho_{Cu} = 8.9\times10^3$, $\sigma_{oil} = 1.5\times10^3$ kg/m³. $\eta = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9v_t} = \dfrac{2(4\times10^{-6})(7.4\times10^3)(9.8)}{9(0.065)} \approx 0.99$ Pa s.

Molecules at a liquid's surface have neighbours only on one side, so the surface behaves like a stretched membrane. Surface tension S is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, or equally the extra energy per unit area of surface (N/m = J/m²).

Water wets clean glass ($\theta \approx 0^\circ$) and rises; mercury ($\theta \approx 140^\circ$) is depressed. Worked example: in a glass tube of radius 0.5 mm, water ($S = 0.073$ N/m) rises $h = \dfrac{2(0.073)}{1000(9.8)(5\times10^{-4})} = \dfrac{0.146}{4.9} \approx 0.030$ m $= 3.0$ cm.

problem.en: How high does water rise in a clean glass capillary of radius 0.5 mm? (S = 0.073 N m⁻¹, θ = 0°, ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. How high does water rise in a clean glass capillary of radius 0.5 mm? (S = 0.073 N m⁻¹, θ = 0°, ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)

say.en: Let us solve this together. How high does water rise in a clean glass capillary of radius 0.5 millimetres? (S equals 0.073 newtons m to the power minus 1, theta equals 0 degrees, rho equals 1000 kilograms m to the power minus 3, g equals 9.8 metres s to the power minus 2).
h equals 2S cos theta /rho gr, with cos 0 degrees equals 1.
h equals 2 times 0.073 / (1000 times 9.8 times 0.5 times 10 to the power minus 3) equals 0.146 divided by 4.9.
h is approximately 0.030 metres.
So the answer is About 3 centimetres.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. The work done in blowing a soap bubble of radius 1 centimetre (surface tension 0.03 newtons m to the power minus 1) is about.
A soap bubble has two surfaces, so delta A equals 2 times 4 pi r squared.
W equals S times 8 pi r squared equals 0.03 times 8 pi times 10 to the power minus 4 is approximately 7.54e-05 joules.

homework.en: Find the excess pressure inside a water drop of radius 1 mm (S = 0.072 N m⁻¹).

narration.en: Recap. Surface tension S = F/l = surface energy per unit area. Excess pressure: drop 2S/r, soap bubble 4S/r. Capillary rise h = 2S cos θ/(ρgr). θ < 90° wets the solid; mercury (θ > 90°) is depressed.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಎಳೆತ S = F/l = ಏಕಮಾನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣದ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಶಕ್ತಿ. ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಒತ್ತಡ: ಹನಿ 2S/r, ಗುಳ್ಳೆ 4S/r. ಲೋಮನಾಳ ಏರಿಕೆ h = 2S cos θ/(ρgr). θ < 90° ತೇವಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಪಾದರಸ ಕೆಳಗಿಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Surface tension S equals F over l equals surface energy per unit area.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಎಳೆತ S equals F over l equals ಏಕಮಾನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣದ ಮೇಲ್ಮೈ ಶಕ್ತಿ.

say.en: Excess pressure: drop 2S/r, soap bubble 4S/r.
Capillary rise h equals 2S cos theta /rho gr.
say.kn: ಲೋಮನಾಳ ಏರಿಕೆ h equals 2S cos theta /rho gr.

say.en: theta < 90 degrees wets the solid; mercury (theta > 90 degrees) is depressed.
